change_summary: Reference baseline for all future comparisons.
notes: Current baseline run stored in outputs/vn30f1m_outputs_version1. Cost model locked. If rerun, append a new row with the same scenario_id and increment run_number.

change_summary: Raise short entry threshold from 0.30 to 0.33 to reduce taxed short entries.
notes: Decoder TFT degraded versus baseline: lower return, lower Sharpe, higher drawdown, higher turnover. Short-entry tightening alone is not a good next direction for decoder_tft.

change_summary: Restore mild asymmetry thresholds after rejecting short-entry-only tightening.
notes: Mild asymmetry is better than s01 for decoder_tft, but still below the baseline on return and Sharpe. Keep it as a reference only until the next TFT hyperparameter sweep.

change_summary: Decoder TFT hyperparameter sweep: sequence_length 156 vs 390, hidden_size 64, dropout 0.2, learning_rate 1e-4, batch_size 64.
notes: Decoder TFT improved materially versus s02: higher return, higher Sharpe, lower drawdown, and lower turnover. Decoder Transformer also stayed strong; LSTM remained the most defensive deep model.

change_summary: Fix decoder_tft to the short sequence baseline: sequence_length 156 with hidden_size 64, dropout 0.2, learning_rate 1e-4, batch_size 64.
notes: Short-sequence TFT underperformed s03 on return and Sharpe, but reduced turnover and drawdown. LSTM became very defensive; Decoder Transformer stayed positive but weaker than s03.

change_summary: TFT hyperparameter sweep: increase sequence_length from 156 to 390 while keeping hidden_size 64, dropout 0.2, learning_rate 1e-4, and batch_size 64 fixed.
notes: s05 is a clear regression versus s04. Long sequence_length=390 hurt decoder_tft materially: lower return, lower Sharpe, deeper drawdown, and lower-quality trading. Reject this direction and keep s04 as the better TFT reference.

change_summary: Reduce decoder_tft hidden_size from 64 to 32 while keeping sequence_length 156, dropout 0.2, learning_rate 1e-4, and batch_size 64 fixed.
notes: s06 is rejected. Smaller hidden_size=32 did not improve decoder_tft; it stayed highly exposed, produced negative return and Sharpe, and did not solve the signal quality problem.

change_summary: Add decoder_tft_turnover_penalty_lambda=0.05 to the TFT training loss while keeping sequence_length 156, hidden_size 64, dropout 0.2, learning_rate 1e-4, and batch_size 64 fixed.
notes: s07 is not promoted. Turnover penalty improved decoder_tft versus s06, but total return and Sharpe remain negative. It suggests noisy turnover is part of the problem, but the signal edge is still too weak.

change_summary: Keep TFT hyperparameters fixed and restrict model inputs to a clean trend subset: returns, normalized returns, volatility, EMA trend, MACD(32,96) core/enriched features, ATR, cyclical time context, and trade_allowed.
notes: s09 is promoted. Decoder TFT improved sharply versus s08 and now clears the working research goal on both annual return and Sharpe, with much better turnover quality than earlier broad-feature runs.

change_summary: Keep the s09 clean_trend subset and TFT hyperparameters fixed, but select TFT checkpoints by validation score: valid_loss + 0.05 * valid_turnover_proxy.
notes: s10 is promoted and becomes the new lead scenario. Decoder TFT improved materially versus s09 on total return, Sharpe, and drawdown while turnover stayed essentially unchanged, supporting the stricter validation checkpoint selection rule.

change_summary: Keep the current full-sell-tax execution setup and clean_trend subset, but select decoder_tft checkpoints with side-aware penalties: valid_loss + 0.05 * turnover + 0.03 * buy_turnover + 0.08 * sell_turnover.
notes: s12 slightly improved decoder_tft versus s11 on return, Sharpe, and drawdown, but only marginally. Side-aware validation selection helped behavior control more than alpha creation under the full sell-side tax regime.

change_summary: Keep the full-sell-tax execution setup, clean_trend subset, and side-aware validation selection, but upgrade decoder_tft to multitask learning with auxiliary future realized volatility and volatility-regime targets.
notes: s13 is the first meaningful recovery after the full sell-side tax deterioration. Decoder TFT improved clearly versus s12 on return, Sharpe, and average net pnl per trade, suggesting the multitask vol/regime representation adds useful alpha quality, though it still trails the best baseline and lstm_dmn on robustness.

change_summary: Keep the s13 multitask decoder_tft and side-aware validation selection, but scale the raw TFT signal by predicted high-volatility regime probability before threshold execution, using low_vol_scale=1.00 and high_vol_scale=0.60.
notes: s14a is promoted over s13 on the full sell-side tax branch. Decoder TFT improved materially on return, Sharpe, turnover efficiency, and average net pnl per trade, validating regime-conditioned exposure as a stronger direction than further threshold tuning, though drawdown worsened slightly versus s13.

change_summary: Keep s14a regime-conditioned exposure, but make high-volatility scaling asymmetric by side: long high-vol scale 0.85, short high-vol scale 0.45, while keeping low-vol scales at 1.00.
notes: s15 is rejected. Asymmetric regime scaling reduced turnover and improved drawdown, but it cut too much useful short exposure: decoder_tft return, Sharpe, and average net pnl per trade all deteriorated sharply versus s14a.

change_summary: Keep the s14a regime-conditioned exposure framework, but reduce decoder_tft multitask weights to vol=0.05 and regime=0.05 while returning to symmetric high-vol scaling.
notes: s16a is rejected. Lowering the volatility auxiliary weight hurt decoder_tft materially versus s14a: return, Sharpe, average net pnl per trade, and drawdown all worsened. This suggests the stronger volatility supervision in s13/s14a was useful rather than overweighted.

change_summary: Keep the s14a regime-conditioned exposure framework and multitask weights, but add asymmetric train-loss penalties for decoder_tft: buy_turnover_lambda=0.01 and sell_turnover_lambda=0.05.
notes: s17 is not promoted. It improved decoder_tft Sharpe and drawdown dramatically, but became too defensive: turnover collapsed, flat time rose to nearly 80%, and return stayed too low. Treat it as proof that side-aware train loss can control risk, but not as the lead branch scenario.

change_summary: Keep the s14a regime-conditioned exposure framework and vol auxiliary weight at 0.10, but increase decoder_tft regime auxiliary loss weight from 0.05 to 0.10 while leaving train-loss turnover penalties off.
notes: s18 is rejected. Stronger regime classification supervision hurt materially versus s14a: return, Sharpe, and average net pnl per trade all deteriorated, while the lower drawdown only reflected a weaker, more passive model. s14a remains the promoted branch scenario.

change_summary: Keep the s14a regime-conditioned exposure framework and current multitask vol/regime losses, but add a downside-risk auxiliary target: target_future_downside_semivariance_12 with decoder_tft_aux_downside_loss_weight = 0.05.
notes: s19 improved decoder_tft trade quality versus s14a on drawdown, turnover, and average net pnl per trade, but did not beat s14a on total return or aggregate Sharpe. Keep it as a credible alternative risk-shaped branch, not the promoted scenario.
